questions.enonce_markdown: State the coordinates of the point B. (1 mark)
questions.corrige_markdown:
B is where the curve meets the $x$-axis other than at O, so $y = 0$:
$$2x(3 - x) = 0 \;\Longrightarrow\; x = 0 \ (\text{point O}) \quad\text{or}\quad x = 3.$$
$$\boxed{B = (3, 0)}$$

questions.enonce_markdown: Show that the value of $k$ is $\dfrac52$. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
D $= (k, k)$ lies on the curve $y = 2x(3 - x)$, so its coordinates satisfy the equation:
$$k = 2k(3 - k).$$
D is not the origin (it lies above the $x$-axis, with $k > 0$), so $k \neq 0$ and we may divide by $k$:
$$1 = 2(3 - k) = 6 - 2k \;\Longrightarrow\; 2k = 5 \;\Longrightarrow\; k = \tfrac52. \qquad \blacksquare$$
So $D = \left(\tfrac52, \tfrac52\right)$.

questions.enonce_markdown: Find an equation of the straight line passing through D and E. (3 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
$E = (0, 5)$ and $D = \left(\tfrac52, \tfrac52\right)$. The gradient is
$$m = \frac{\tfrac52 - 5}{\tfrac52 - 0} = \frac{-\tfrac52}{\tfrac52} = -1.$$
The line crosses the $y$-axis at $E(0, 5)$, so its equation is $y = -x + 5$.
$$\boxed{y = 5 - x \quad (\text{equivalently } x + y = 5)}$$
**Check:** D satisfies it, since $\tfrac52 + \tfrac52 = 5$.

questions.enonce_markdown: Show that the $x$-coordinates of the point C is 1. (3 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
C and D are the points where the line and the curve meet, so equate $y$:
$$2x(3 - x) = 5 - x \;\Longrightarrow\; 6x - 2x^2 = 5 - x \;\Longrightarrow\; 2x^2 - 7x + 5 = 0 \;\Longrightarrow\; (2x - 5)(x - 1) = 0.$$
So $x = \tfrac52$ or $x = 1$. The root $x = \tfrac52$ is the $x$-coordinate of D (part (b)); the other intersection point is C, so the $x$-coordinate of C is $1$. $\blacksquare$

(Then $y_C = 5 - 1 = 4$, so $C = (1, 4)$; check on the curve: $2(1)(3 - 1) = 4$.)

questions.enonce_markdown: Calculate the area of the region R bounded by the curve $y = 2x(3 - x)$ and line DE. (4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Between C ($x = 1$) and D ($x = \tfrac52$) the curve lies above the line (for example at $x = 2$: curve $y = 4$, line $y = 3$). So
$$\text{Area} = \int_1^{5/2}\big[2x(3 - x) - (5 - x)\big]\,dx = \int_1^{5/2}\left(-2x^2 + 7x - 5\right)dx.$$
Integrate:
$$\left[-\frac{2x^3}{3} + \frac{7x^2}{2} - 5x\right]_1^{5/2}.$$
At $x = \tfrac52$: $-\tfrac{2}{3}\cdot\tfrac{125}{8} + \tfrac72\cdot\tfrac{25}{4} - \tfrac{25}{2} = -\tfrac{125}{12} + \tfrac{175}{8} - \tfrac{25}{2} = \dfrac{-250 + 525 - 300}{24} = -\dfrac{25}{24}$.

At $x = 1$: $-\tfrac23 + \tfrac72 - 5 = \dfrac{-4 + 21 - 30}{6} = -\dfrac{13}{6} = -\dfrac{52}{24}$.

$$\text{Area} = -\frac{25}{24} - \left(-\frac{52}{24}\right) = \frac{27}{24} = \frac98.$$
$$\boxed{\text{Area of } R = \tfrac98 = 1.125 \text{ square units}}$$

**Check:** the area between a parabola with leading coefficient $-2$ and a chord is $\dfrac{|a|\,(x_D - x_C)^3}{6} = \dfrac{2\left(\tfrac32\right)^3}{6} = \dfrac{27/4}{6} = \tfrac98$.
